name: Release Candidate Preparation
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read
concurrency:
  group: candidate-preparation-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
jobs:
  qualify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    env:
      PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE: '1'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Verify qualified source checkout
        env:
          QUALIFICATION_SOURCE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
        run: |
          test "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$QUALIFICATION_SOURCE"
          printf 'QUALIFIED_SOURCE_COMMIT=%s\n' "$QUALIFICATION_SOURCE"
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020
        with:
          node-version: 22.23.2
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm --prefix hardhat ci
      - name: Source and dependency compatibility boundaries
        id: source-policy
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          manifest_sha=$(sha256sum config/manager-dependency-maintenance-v1.json | cut -d' ' -f1)
          verifier_sha=$(sha256sum scripts/release/maintenance-profile.py | cut -d' ' -f1)
          python3 scripts/release/maintenance-profile.py --dependency-root "$(realpath node_modules)"
          printf 'manifest=%s\nverifier=%s\n' "$manifest_sha" "$verifier_sha" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Run root and Hardhat audits at low threshold
        run: |
          npm audit --audit-level=low
          npm --prefix hardhat audit --audit-level=low
      - name: Compile reviewed candidate contracts
        run: npm run build
      - name: Complete preflight and real entrypoint regressions
        run: npm --prefix hardhat run test:preflight
      - name: Native compiler, provider, storage and historical runtime compatibility
        run: npm --prefix hardhat run test:registry-native
      - name: Check bytecode sizes
        run: npm run size
      - name: Verify active guide and metadata alignment
        run: npm run docs:check
      - name: Test release qualification gates offline
        run: |
          python3 scripts/release/test-release-gates.py
          python3 scripts/release/run-maintenance-inherited-tests.py --dependency-root "$(realpath node_modules)"
      - name: Native transformation profile and inherited release tests
        run: |
          python3 scripts/release/test-maintenance-profile.py
          python3 scripts/release/test-maintenance-qualification.py
          python3 scripts/release/test-transformational-qualification.py
          python3 scripts/release/test-publication-authorization-ti.py
          python3 scripts/release/test-pages-publication-maintenance.py
          python3 scripts/release/test-maintenance-plumbing.py
      - name: Resolve candidate identity from package metadata
        id: candidate
        run: |
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import os, re, sys
          sys.path.insert(0, 'scripts/release')
          from release_common import TAG
          if not re.fullmatch(r'v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+', TAG):
              raise ValueError('Unsupported release tag')
          with open(os.environ['GITHUB_OUTPUT'], 'a') as output:
              output.write(f'tag={TAG}\n')
          PY
      - name: Build and independently rebuild candidate assets
        env:
          CANDIDATE_MANIFEST_SHA: ${{ steps.source-policy.outputs.manifest }}
          CANDIDATE_VERIFIER_SHA: ${{ steps.source-policy.outputs.verifier }}
        run: |
          for output in "build/release/${{ steps.candidate.outputs.tag }}-candidate" /tmp/agi-candidate-rebuild; do
            python3 scripts/release/package-release.py --out "$output" \
              --profile manager-dependency-maintenance-v1 --object-store "$PWD" \
              --dependency-root "$(realpath node_modules)" \
              --manifest config/manager-dependency-maintenance-v1.json \
              --manifest-sha256 "$CANDIDATE_MANIFEST_SHA" \
              --verifier-sha256 "$CANDIDATE_VERIFIER_SHA"
          done
          diff -r "build/release/${{ steps.candidate.outputs.tag }}-candidate" /tmp/agi-candidate-rebuild
      - name: Clean extraction and offline smoke test
        env:
          CANDIDATE_MANIFEST_SHA: ${{ steps.source-policy.outputs.manifest }}
          CANDIDATE_VERIFIER_SHA: ${{ steps.source-policy.outputs.verifier }}
        run: |
          python3 scripts/release/verify-package.py "build/release/${{ steps.candidate.outputs.tag }}-candidate" \
            --profile manager-dependency-maintenance-v1 --manifest config/manager-dependency-maintenance-v1.json \
            --manifest-sha256 "$CANDIDATE_MANIFEST_SHA" \
            --verifier-sha256 "$CANDIDATE_VERIFIER_SHA"
      - name: Retain source-pinned candidate assets
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a
        with:
          name: AGIJobManager-${{ steps.candidate.outputs.tag }}-candidate-${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
          path: build/release/${{ steps.candidate.outputs.tag }}-candidate/
          if-no-files-found: error
# Deliberately no publish job and no contents:write permission.
# Publication needs separately reviewed final-source CI metadata and authorization.

    types: [completed]

# AGI Jobs — Your next idea starts here

<!-- Generated by scripts/docs/current-release.mjs. Edit its template, then run npm run docs:gen. -->

[![Your next idea starts here. A website, a presentation or a clear report. Une idée suffit pour commencer.](site/assets/start-here.svg)](https://montrealai.github.io/AGIJobManager/employers/)

**Latest reported mainnet deployment:** [17 October Manager and authority record](docs/deployments/MAINNET_MANAGER_2026-10-17.md). Manager `0x3a9B3A0712e066de4265404Fa5ff4171fE29a3F8`; intake paused, identity configuration unlocked. Earlier instances and their claims remain separate.

**Latest retained ENS configuration:** [19 October snapshot and fee/source-review limitations](docs/deployments/ENS_CONFIGURATION_RETAINED_2026-10-19.md). Helper `0xBaC826CF5f169EA168A23173F3DbBdA7Ed953400`, root `usdc.jobs.agi.eth`, prefix `job-v2-`; historical block `26,227,598` at `2026-10-19T15:44:23Z`. This is not a current-state or activation claim.

## What would you like done?

A simple website. A presentation. A clear report. Begin with your idea and prepare a request for AI workers, one step at a time. You do not need to install software or understand the code in this repository.

### [Start my request →](https://montrealai.github.io/AGIJobManager/employers/) · [Commencer ma demande →](https://montrealai.github.io/AGIJobManager/fr/employers/)

**Free to prepare · No sign-up · No wallet needed to start**

1. **Choose an example.** Pick the result closest to your idea, or describe something else.
2. **Make it yours.** Say what you need, choose a proposed budget and decide how to check the work.
3. **Keep your request.** Download it, print it, or save it in this browser and come back later.

Use **Larger text** if that makes reading more comfortable. The guided page has everyday words, large buttons and editable examples in English and French. Nothing is posted or paid for while you prepare your request.

**En français :** [Commencez ici](https://montrealai.github.io/AGIJobManager/fr/employers/). Choisissez un exemple, décrivez votre idée, puis enregistrez ou imprimez votre demande. La préparation est gratuite, sans inscription. Le bouton **Texte agrandi** facilite la lecture.

**When you are ready to publish:** a separate, advanced screen handles posting and payment. It currently requires a digital wallet, USDC for the job and ETH for Ethereum fees; there is no card checkout. Verify the operator and availability before funding. Preparing a request does not reserve a worker or guarantee a result. [Read the full employer guide](docs/ui/EMPLOYER_ONBOARDING.md).

[Explore the AGI Jobs website](https://montrealai.github.io/AGIJobManager/) · [Site en français](https://montrealai.github.io/AGIJobManager/fr/) · [Participant and operator guides](docs/START_HERE.md) · [Current USDC console](https://montrealai.github.io/AGIJobManager/agijobmanager-usdc.html)

## SUCCESSOR Ω Builder for everyone

Create a small working system, inspect its files, try a measured improvement, choose the version you want and download a copy you can restore. The free local path runs in your browser without an account, installation, wallet or provider key.

**[Open the Builder](https://montrealai.github.io/AGIJobManager/successor/)** · **[Ouvrir le Créateur](https://montrealai.github.io/AGIJobManager/fr/successor/)** · [Guide and reproducible walkthrough](docs/successor/README.md).

Two bounded local engines produce real editable artifacts: a public-data report with exact decimal totals, and a static website with semantic structure and optional section navigation. They use reviewed deterministic code. Custom missions can be specified and exported; their execution remains unavailable until a suitable runtime is commissioned. Local checks, independent qualification, payment and permission remain separate.

**En français :** créez un rapport de données publiques ou un site simple, vérifiez le résultat, choisissez une amélioration et téléchargez votre système. Le parcours local fonctionne sans compte, portefeuille ni clé de fournisseur. [Guide français](docs/successor/GUIDE_FR.md).

## Inspect a transformation campaign

The retained v1.19.5 developer adapter inspects a complete Alpha transformation campaign with an installed, compatible native inspector and independently supplied runtime bindings. The current native pilot has zero currency allowances: **inspection is free; a positive paid proposal is unsupported**. Inspection does not execute work, grant permissions or sign a transaction. The existing local Builder and its pinned runtime remain unchanged. Start with the [v1.19.6 guide](docs/releases/v1.19.6/START_HERE.md) and [adapter contract and recovery](docs/successor/TRANSFORMATIONAL_WORK.md). This is a developer API, not a new console action.

**En français :** l’inspection d’une campagne Alpha reste gratuite, sans permission d’exécution ni paiement. Le pilote natif à plafond zéro ne permet aucune proposition payante. Le Créateur local existant reste inchangé.

## Historical October 10 instance — ENS connected, activation on HOLD

The 10 October 2026 [deployment and connection record](docs/deployments/MAINNET_USDC_2026-10-10.md) reports the verified helper at `0x6EE7A600C56C1Bfd12c482190d5dAbDD7194CDBC` connected to manager `0xCFA78f9980eA9B55c705B3E44467baE383cE1fA7`, using **`job-<jobId>.usdc.jobs.agi.eth`**. At the recorded block **26,165,026**, intake was paused and no job had been posted. This is dated operator evidence, not a live status indicator or permission to fund jobs.

**Production activation remains on HOLD.** The [activation review and five closeout gates](docs/OPERATIONS/PRODUCTION_ACTIVATION.md) are separate from successful deployment. The proposed 100-USDC commissioning ceiling is a draft, not an applied setting. Default console/deployment addresses remain blank; no automatic connection, approval, funding or unpause is introduced.

**En français :** l’intégration ENS est vérifiée dans le relevé daté, mais l’ouverture des travaux payants reste suspendue. Ce relevé ne constitue ni un état en temps réel ni une autorisation de paiement.

## Ideas behind the work

[Read four selected essays](https://montrealai.github.io/AGIJobManager/#reading) on choosing workers, public work history and delivery evidence. Each article links to its current guide. [Reading notes and version context](docs/READING.md) · Articles en anglais, résumés français disponibles.

## For developers, operators and release reviewers

AGIJobManager is the software behind the USDC job contract and supporting tools. The technical documentation, qualification evidence and deployment instructions follow below. [Website publishing guide](docs/ui/GITHUB_PAGES.md).

**Current software version: v1.19.6 — Scoped dependency maintenance candidate.**
[Latest deployment and instance-specific operations](docs/OPERATIONS/COMMISSIONING.md) ·
[Finite operator actions](OPERATOR_ACTIONS_REQUIRED.md) · [Release notes](docs/releases/v1.19.6/RELEASE_NOTES.md).

**[previously published v1.19.5 COMPLETE ZIP](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGIJobManager/releases/download/v1.19.5/AGIJobManager-v1.19.5-COMPLETE.zip)** · [previously published v1.19.5 qualification](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGIJobManager/releases/download/v1.19.5/QUALIFICATION.json).
Check [release and download availability for v1.19.6](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGIJobManager/releases/tag/v1.19.6). Published assets identify their exact source; later main-branch work requires separate qualification.
Software publication and intake activation are separate decisions.

AGI Jobs covers work a person or team can do using a keyboard, mouse and screen. Employers define the result and acceptance criteria; AGI Agents perform the work; AGI Nodes independently validate the delivered result. AGIJobManager provides the on-chain job lifecycle, USDC escrow, bonded voting, dispute outcomes and payment recovery. Computer execution and judging the work happen outside the contract.

**New automated work uses operator budgets without retainers.** Agent/Node admission requires schema 6; employer funding requires schema 7; both require `reviewPayment: operator-budget`. Existing retainer credits, refunds and journals remain recoverable. Use [no-retainer operations](docs/OPERATIONS/NO_RETAINERS.md) and the [current admission reference](docs/OPERATIONS/QUALIFIED_ADMISSION.md). The manual console and permissionless contract do not enforce these private admission policies.

## Learn from measured outcomes

This edition tightens [operating qualification](docs/OPERATIONS/OPERATING_QUALIFICATION.md): each held-out job class must meet loss-rate and supervision limits as well as separate Agent/Node cash floors. The [project economics planner](docs/OPERATIONS/PROJECT_ECONOMICS.md) accounts for unpaid intermediate stages, failed work, deposits and each participant's capital. Examples at $100, $1,000 and $10,000 are explicitly assumptions. Use the [bounded pilot guide](docs/OPERATIONS/VALUE_TIER_PILOT.md) to replace those assumptions with real-machine evidence. Private companions also reject stale desktop observations after a failed refresh.

The [Astra review pilot](docs/OPERATIONS/ASTRA_REVIEW_PILOT.md) shows why reviewer participation can fail a job that otherwise passes modeled work checks. Its offline scheduler reserves three independent reviewer windows across competing jobs; its pilot audit keeps completion, supervision, Agent/Node losses, settlement defects and judgment errors separate. The study is synthetic, and neither tool authorizes live intake.

## Choose your starting point

| You want to | Open |
| --- | --- |
| Prepare and post your first job | [Employer onboarding page](https://montrealai.github.io/AGIJobManager/employers/) and [draft-to-funding guide](docs/ui/EMPLOYER_ONBOARDING.md) |
| Perform or review a job | [Participant start guide](docs/START_HERE.md) and [USDC console guide](docs/ui/GENESIS_JOB_MAINNET_HTML_UI.md) |
| Describe general computer work and validation | [Computer-work specification and current coverage](docs/OPERATIONS/GENERAL_COMPUTER_WORK.md) |
| Run private Agents, Nodes or supporting services | [Private companion setup and compatibility](docs/OPERATIONS/PRIVATE_FLEET.md) |
| Deploy or operate a manager | [Hardhat guide](hardhat/README.md), [checked commands](docs/RELEASE_GUIDE.md) and [launch checklist](docs/LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md) |
| Recover a job or unpaid claim | [Settlement and recovery guide](docs/OPERATIONS/SETTLEMENT_RECOVERY.md) |
| Review the implementation and evidence | [Release scope](docs/V1_RELEASE_SCOPE.md), [testing](docs/TESTING.md) and [mainnet readiness](docs/MAINNET_READINESS.md) |

## What is implemented

| Layer | Included behavior | Operational boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Public protocol | Native six-decimal USDC, escrow, Agent bonds, Node votes, buyer acceptance, disputes, refunds and protected failed payments | A transaction and verified resulting state establish settlement; time passing alone sends no payment |
| General job specification | Goals, inputs, native output files, acceptance/evidence criteria, permissions, budgets, deadlines and runtime hashes | A job description does not install missing applications or prove task competence |
| Admission tools | Signed action-bound qualification, calibrated economics, canonical RPC observations and separate capital/cost/capacity limits | `checkNewWork` is the current boundary; historical `checkAdmission` analysis does not authorize new work |
| Private execution | Role-specific model and sandbox checks, bounded processing, complete execution windows, independent review workspaces and durable attempts | Public jobs use an isolated desktop. The new private native runner controls dedicated signed-in Mac accounts through encrypted, signed task packets; actual Mac commissioning remains required |
| Workforce qualification | Exact source/runtime identities, signed Mac commissioning, independent validation, reconciled costs, cash settlements and external review evidence | Missing or expired evidence blocks production native execution; signatures establish attested provenance, not truth |
| Supporting private services | Employer, Evidence, Moderator and Recovery services; exception and human-time records | Automated decisions require supported criteria and reviewed standing authority |

This source documents the compatibility baseline **Fleet 1.10.0, Agent 1.16.0 and Node 2.17.0**; newer private editions are tracked separately. They are separate private downloads with offline HTML guides and Mac launchers, not files in this public repository. The [companion guide](docs/OPERATIONS/PRIVATE_FLEET.md) explains the M1/M2 setup, upgrade procedure and actual commissioning requirements.

Use the [workforce qualification guide](docs/OPERATIONS/WORKFORCE_QUALIFICATION.md) to assess operational readiness. Native/private task execution is a separate workflow: it does not load a wallet, publish private plaintext, or automatically submit encrypted jobs and signed votes to the public manager. See the companion guide for this integration boundary.

## One job, from specification to payment

1. The employer defines the deliverables and independently checkable acceptance criteria, then posts the agreed USDC amount.
2. An eligible Agent checks the job, obtains any required bond allowance and takes the assignment.
3. The Agent completes the work and submits its delivery URI before the applicable deadline.
4. Eligible independent Nodes inspect the actual result and vote within the review period. Missing or uncertain evidence must not become invented approval.
5. The appropriate caller settles, disputes, expires or refunds the job under its actual state and deadlines. Failed outgoing transfers remain reserved for the original beneficiary to claim.

Read [buyer protection](docs/BUYER_PROTECTION.md), the [participant guide](docs/USERS.md) and [protocol flow](docs/PROTOCOL_FLOW.md) for all outcomes. The private project coordinator schedules separately admitted Agent/Node stages and binds independently accepted inputs. It does not implement atomic project settlement; see [confidential project work](docs/OPERATIONS/CONFIDENTIAL_PROJECT_WORK.md).

## Payments and identity

Successful jobs pay the validator allocation first (**8% default**), then **30% of the original job cost to wallet one**, **10% to wallet two**, and the remainder to the Agent. When the full default reviewer allocation is paid, a 100 USDC job pays 8 / 30 / 10 / 52. Buyer acceptance with zero validators instead pays 0 / 30 / 10 / 60, excluding separate bond returns; the reviewer budget is shared, not paid once per reviewer. The validator percentage is fixed when each job is posted. Bonds, slashing and refunds are separate; [the payout specification](docs/USDC_PAYOUT_SPLIT.md) defines rounding and all branches.

Agents normally use `*.agent.agi.eth` or `*.alpha.agent.agi.eth`; Nodes use `*.club.agi.eth` or `*.alpha.club.agi.eth`. Configured allowlist/Merkle exceptions also exist. **NFT eligibility is disabled by default** on fresh managers and is separate from role membership. Read [identity and proofs](docs/guides/IDENTITY_AND_PROOFS.md) and [NFT policy](docs/NFT_POLICY.md).

The generic fresh-deployment script uses `job-<jobId>.usdc-<chainId>-<manager40>.alpha.jobs.agi.eth`; this is a tooling policy, not a required contract suffix. The separately commissioned instance uses `job-<jobId>.usdc.jobs.agi.eth`. Existing managers preserve their recorded namespace and labels. [ENS naming policy](docs/ENS_DEPLOYMENT_NAMESPACES.md) describes ownership and wiring.

## Install and verify the public source

**Existing production checkout:** preserve its saved artifacts, original receipts and working patches. For the historical October 10 instance, use its [read-only connection command](docs/deployments/MAINNET_USDC_2026-10-10.md#read-only-commands). For the October 17 Manager, use the [latest record and original instance evidence](docs/deployments/MAINNET_MANAGER_2026-10-17.md); do not pull, reinstall, compile or redeploy there merely to consume this documentation update. The installation commands below are for a separate development checkout.

Use Node.js >=22.23.2 and the committed lockfiles. From the repository root:

```bash
npm ci
npm --prefix hardhat ci
npm run build
npm run size
npm test
npm run docs:check
```

For deployment, first run `npm --prefix hardhat run setup`, review the private configuration, then use the [Hardhat procedure](hardhat/README.md). New managers start with intake paused. The [default configuration](config/usdc-deployment.json) still auto-selects **no live manager**. The [October 17 Manager record](config/mainnet/manager-8815-2026-10-17.json) and [historical October 10 instance](config/mainnet/agi-jobs-usdc.json) identify separate deployments; neither is a replacement default or an activation grant. Publishing this software does not deploy contracts or open intake.

The current manager uses eight fixed linked libraries. The [integrated source](docs/qualification/INTEGRATED_CANDIDATE_20261017.md) includes explicit-governor constructors, bounded creator preflight recovery and a source-pinned compiler optimizer mitigation. The v1.19.6 wrapper requires fresh exact-final-source qualification. Earlier [ENS membership hardening](docs/qualification/ENS_MEMBERSHIP_REVOCATION.md), payout rules and historical deployment records remain preserved. Existing immutable managers are not upgraded by this software release; preserve their original source, jobs and recovery paths. Use the [second-deployment checklist](docs/DEPLOYMENT/SECOND_MAINNET_RELEASE.md) and [compatibility guide](docs/V1_RELEASE_SCOPE.md#compatibility).

## Release evidence and production use

The release archive records the qualified source, all required CI results, per-file hashes and reproducible assets. Checks cover contract behavior, security analysis, UI/browser behavior, documentation and historical native-USDC forks. These establish behavior for tested cases, not universal work quality, independent audit, actual M1/M2 throughput or profitability.

Commission the actual deployment, machines, providers, independent participants, recovery and operator workload before production intake. [Current computer-use integrations](docs/OPERATIONS/COMPUTER_USE_CURRENT.md) distinguish available vendor capabilities from the adapter shipped here. Model changes require fresh runtime qualification.

## Documentation

[Documentation hub](docs/README.md) · [Worked lifecycle](docs/QUINTESSENTIAL_USE_CASE.md) · [Complete npm command inventory](docs/REFERENCE/COMMANDS.md) · [Script reference](docs/SCRIPTS_REFERENCE.md) · [Security policy](SECURITY.md) · [Legal and privacy notices](docs/LEGAL/README.md) · [MIT license](LICENSE).

Maintain generated guides with `npm run docs:gen`; verify them with `npm run docs:check`. The `check-no-binaries` policy is exposed as `npm run check:no-binaries`. Current release labels, download labels, schemas and commands are checked alongside generated content. Historical release and qualification records retain their original identities.

# v1.19.6 maintenance qualification and operating boundaries

The v1.19.6 maintenance candidate patches only the reviewed follow-redirects, Hono and Vite resolutions and software labels, with a separate finite source policy. Its exact-source hosted qualification remains pending. This document grants no deployment or intake authority.

The retained v1.19.5 source adds [free native transformation-campaign inspection](successor/TRANSFORMATIONAL_WORK.md) and a separate finite source policy. The native pilot has zero currency allowances; positive paid proposals remain unsupported. Its [validation record](releases/v1.19.5/VALIDATION.md) distinguishes local checks from pending exact-final-source qualification. This adapter changes no deployed contract, intake setting, Builder code pin, compiler behavior or dependency resolution. It does not establish independent review or live readiness.

Latest deployment: see the [17 October Manager record](deployments/MAINNET_MANAGER_2026-10-17.md) for the reported nine finalized creations, mixed explorer-match results, governor/moderator and paused/unlocked configuration. This dated evidence does not establish current full readiness or paid-intake approval.

Latest retained configuration: the [19 October ENS addendum](deployments/ENS_CONFIGURATION_RETAINED_2026-10-19.md) records helper `0xBaC826CF5f169EA168A23173F3DbBdA7Ed953400`, root `usdc.jobs.agi.eth` and prefix `job-v2-` at block `26,227,598` (`2026-10-19T15:44:23Z`). Its 27 state comparisons pass; its fee-ceiling exception and separate unresolved explorer source-input match remain explicit. The block timestamp is separately established historical metadata, not a new current-state readback or the original checker's unknown observation time.

Version 1.19.4 is a prepared software correction for hidden creator-key input, public-only mission validation, recoverable Computer Use history and separately priced unsigned USDC proposals. Disposable acceptance executes captured native-inspector code; software and Pages publication require exact-source qualification. See the [prepared v1.19.4 release notes](releases/v1.19.4/RELEASE_NOTES.md) and [v1.19.4 preparation snapshot](releases/v1.19.4/START_HERE.md). These guides are not qualification receipts: all eight final-source workflows, external `QUALIFICATION.json` and the publication workflow must bind the final release source. The correction preserves Solidity, compiler behavior and dependency resolutions from the published v1.19.3 wrapper. Existing deployments remain read-only within this work; deployment, signing, funding, activation and authority changes require separate authorization.

The historical [v1.19.3 release](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGIJobManager/releases/tag/v1.19.3) corrected operator guidance and deployment-evidence presentation around integrated source `8815ed3181778664595f951befd672afbd7a9352`, tree `913e49d65263bc53026916f7fc3b4cbfb93549f8`. That source includes explicit-governor constructors, source-bound creator recovery and the selected compiler optimizer mitigation. Its [historical release notes](releases/v1.19.3/RELEASE_NOTES.md) and [reported mainnet snapshot](releases/v1.19.3/START_HERE.md), the earlier [v1.19.2 release](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGIJobManager/releases/tag/v1.19.2) and dated deployment evidence retain their original identities. Earlier source workflows cannot qualify the v1.19.4 wrapper.

**v1.17.0 software qualification passed; deployment and activation approval remain separate.** Published [v1.17.0](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGIJobManager/releases/tag/v1.17.0) binds source `b721819639668f0074c244d516bbbe0cf57329a7` to its `QUALIFICATION.json` and final-source [contract CI](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGIJobManager/actions/runs/38672184215), [security verification](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGIJobManager/actions/runs/38672184298) and [native-USDC/ENS fork qualification](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGIJobManager/actions/runs/38672184202). These results include the [ENS membership correction](qualification/ENS_MEMBERSHIP_REVOCATION.md), which changes linked library bytecode and requires a new deployment. They do not establish an independent final-source audit, an actual-owner Sepolia rehearsal or readiness of a live instance. Complete the [second-deployment release checklist](DEPLOYMENT/SECOND_MAINNET_RELEASE.md), recording executed checks and explicit owner-accepted omissions separately before a deployment decision. Any later contract, dependency, compiler or linking change requires its own exact-source qualification.

For the planned second deployment, the owner selected no external independent review and no Sepolia rehearsal on 15 October 2026. The [scoped qualification decision](DEPLOYMENT/SECOND_MAINNET_QUALIFICATION_DECISION.md) records both as not performed, with owner-accepted omissions and unchanged technical/authorization gates. AI-assisted review is not an external audit.

For the latest reported deployment, start with the [17 October Manager and authority record](deployments/MAINNET_MANAGER_2026-10-17.md). The [historical October 10 inspection and recovery workflow](OPERATIONS/COMMISSIONING.md#historical-manager-and-ens-helper--10-october-2026) selects only that earlier Manager and its ENS helper; its commands do not inspect the October 17 Manager.

Current automated work uses [operator-budget admission without retainers](OPERATIONS/NO_RETAINERS.md), with schema 6 participant and schema 7 employer policies. Existing credits, refunds and journals remain recoverable. See [general computer work and actual adapter coverage](OPERATIONS/GENERAL_COMPUTER_WORK.md).

v1.14.0 is a software release for verified v0.9.6-compatible managers and new Ethereum deployments. It supplies no live manager, recipient wallets, owner-key verification or production signing authority. Automated qualification is evidence about the pinned source and tested scenarios; it is not an independent audit or a guarantee against every failure.

The project already has a legacy mainnet manager with outstanding original-asset obligations. The [USDC cutover qualification](qualification/USDC_CUTOVER.md) records that live state, the ENS resolver correction first included in v0.9.2 and retained in v1.1.0, and a fork rehearsal preserving existing jobs. Software qualification and live-instance approval remain separate.

The retained [qualified admission tools](OPERATIONS/QUALIFIED_ADMISSION.md) add lifecycle modeling, signed attestations and canonical state reads. A result within supplied limits does not establish live admission readiness or guaranteed participant profitability. Canonical settlement reporting from v1.2.1 remains available.

## Settlement

Jobs, escrow, bonds, rewards and refunds use native Circle USDC with six decimal places. On Ethereum the immutable token is `0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48`, checked against [Circle's address registry](https://developers.circle.com/stablecoins/usdc-contract-addresses).

| Successful 100 USDC job | Default amount |
| --- | ---: |
| Validators, first | 8 USDC |
| First wallet, 30% of original cost | 30 USDC |
| Second wallet, 10% of original cost | 10 USDC |
| Agent, remainder | 52 USDC |

The owner may set the validator budget to 1–60% for newly posted jobs. Existing jobs retain their posting-time percentage. Rounding and unused validator allocations go to the agent. Bonds and slashing are accounted separately. Refund outcomes do not pay the two successful-job wallet shares. Read the [complete payout specification](USDC_PAYOUT_SPLIT.md).

## Retained contract safeguards and qualification

- Intake starts paused in the constructor, eliminating the interval between deployment and a separate pause transaction.
- Job duration settings are bounded to 1–365 days in seconds, preventing owner configuration that can overflow lifecycle deadlines.
- Generic token rescue cannot call the manager itself or USDC. This preserves the boundary around internal completion-NFT minting and reserved funds.
- Deployment checks bind the selected network to its chain ID, validate native USDC and issuer restrictions, enforce compiler and bytecode limits, compare linked runtime code, preserve partial deployment receipts, and report incomplete explorer verification as failure.
- A read-only deployment check verifies the actual instance before opening intake. Current creation assigns the explicit governor atomically with zero pending owner; historical handovers and later voluntary Manager transfers retain two-step acceptance.
- Transaction reviews bind the connected account, network and manager through approvals and submission. Changed contexts require a new review. Failed receipts cannot be reported as successful.
- Qualification includes contract regressions, issuer restrictions, bonds/disputes, exact transfer ordering, fuzzing, concurrent-job invariants, deployment rejection scenarios, browser tests and static-analysis triage.

## Preserved contract qualification scope

Version 1.1.0 adds read-only deployment defaults and corrected operator guidance while retaining v1.0.5 privacy notices, public-content review, credential handling and browser storage. It preserves v1.0.3 ABI, creation/runtime bytecode and disabled NFT default. Existing managers keep their settings, jobs and agreements. See [release scope](V1_RELEASE_SCOPE.md), the [internal contract review](qualification/V1_CONTRACT_REVIEW.md), [v1.0.3 default review](qualification/V103_NFT_DEFAULT.md), [v1.0.4 notice review](qualification/V104_OPERATOR_NOTICES.md), [v1.0.5 privacy review](qualification/V105_PRIVACY.md), [acceptance protocol](V1_ACCEPTANCE.md) and [launch checklist](LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md).

The earlier [v0.9.7 operating review](qualification/OPERATIONS_V097.md) and [v0.9.6 exact-bond review](qualification/BUYER_ECONOMICS_FOLLOWUP.md) remain historical evidence. Full buyer escrow refunds, no-vote dispute escalation, explicit acceptance, full review, credential/controller conflict checks, pause-aware deadlines, neutral timeout and reserved payment claims are preserved. Final source CI and release validation establish the executed qualification scope; independent audit, real-user studies and live-instance readiness are separate evidence.

## Reproduce qualification

Use Node 22.23.2 and the committed lockfiles. Install the root and Hardhat workspaces before running the contract tests; all local tests use disposable accounts. See [dependency scope](DEPENDENCY_SECURITY.md).

```bash
npm ci
npm --prefix hardhat ci
npm test
node scripts/ui/verify-usdc-console.mjs
npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
npm run test:ui:usdc
npm run test:ui
cd hardhat
npm ci
npm run compile
npm run test:preflight
npm run test:deployment
npm run test:mainnet-fork
CUTOVER_REPORT=../build/qualification/mainnet-cutover.json npm run test:cutover
```

The commands above target current source. For the frozen v1.0.0 tag, use its recorded console verifier and qualification commands; it predates the primary-console browser runner. [Release versus source](V1_RELEASE_SCOPE.md#published-download-versus-current-source) identifies the difference. Browser wallet/RPC responses are mocked, with no signing or broadcast.

The qualified fork fixture pins Ethereum block **25,997,388**, hash `0x1495b5decf70b7757b60b8d4ba10d14a7cdb4512f55c4ae5400d8a97b9deedf9`, and checks USDC implementation `0x43506849D7C04F9138D1A2050bbF3A0c054402dd` plus its runtime hash. The v1.17.0 run executes eleven native-USDC cases covering paused launch, exact default-bond settlement, issuer pause/blocklist protected claims and recovery, and reviewer-credit settlement/recovery. Earlier eight-case results remain historical evidence.

The separate cutover fixture pins block **25,998,952**, hash `0xac9075441aff899351bf4ca9abf5be0edc4494b69a1c7543b389fd8cacaa159a`. Its 23 scenarios exercise the actual mainnet ENS contracts, all four participant membership roots and explicit exceptions, separate ownership paths, both NFT modes with unchanged ENS authorization and USDC settlement, further recovery cases, the preserved legacy inventory and the original-asset exit for job 11. See the [source-bound report](qualification/mainnet-cutover.json).

The fork runner exposes only the local Hardhat network. It reads a pinned finalized Ethereum block and executes every transaction on that local fork. It never broadcasts transactions to Ethereum, does not use production private keys and fails if the remote state is unavailable. Fork evidence checks a historical state; USDC implementation and issuer configuration must be rechecked before an actual launch.

```bash
cd ..
FOUNDRY_PROFILE=ci forge build --deny warnings
FOUNDRY_PROFILE=ci forge test
npm run slither
npm run slither:extended
cd ui
npm ci
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run test:e2e
npm run test:a11y
npm run test:headers
```

Use Foundry 1.7.1 and Slither 0.11.6. The extended static-analysis gate preserves raw findings and verifies a reviewed baseline instead of excluding whole detector classes. Consult the linked CI logs and release validation document for exact source-specific results.

## An actual high-stakes launch

Before committing significant funds, obtain independent review of the final source and operational setup, rehearse with the actual owner/signing arrangement on Sepolia, and provide the real recipient addresses. These activities are not completed by publishing a GitHub release.

Complete applicable legal review for the actual operator, owner powers, fee beneficiaries, service scope and jurisdictions. Publish the [operator notice](LEGAL/OPERATOR_NOTICE_TEMPLATE.md) and meet required terms, privacy and language arrangements. A technical readiness report explicitly leaves these matters unassessed; open-source publication and disclaimers do not guarantee regulatory immunity.

Follow the [Hardhat guide](../hardhat/README.md), complete source verification, confirm the constructor-assigned governor and zero pending owner, and run the read-only readiness command while intake remains paused. No current-creation acceptance is required; historical handovers and later voluntary Manager transfers retain their original two-step semantics. Reconcile USDC, both wallets, linked code, policy settings and all reserve counters against the deployment receipt. Open intake only after these instance-specific checks pass; use a deliberately limited first job before increasing exposure.

## Operational limits

- This is not a proxy. Code changes require a new deployment; supported owner settings remain available under their on-chain guards.
- The owner and moderators remain trusted authorities. A compromised owner can misuse eligibility, pause or dispute powers even though reserved funds cannot be withdrawn as surplus.
- Circle may pause USDC, block addresses or upgrade its implementation. Failed outgoing transfers become protected claims; tests establish reserve conservation and same-beneficiary retries. Claims and existing jobs cannot be redirected by rotating wallets.
- Validators can collude or misjudge off-chain work. The employer and assigned agent cannot vote on their own job; duplicate ENS credentials and recorded controllers are rejected. Distinct addresses or ENS names still do not establish independent people or rule out hidden common control. Configure and monitor eligibility accordingly; bonds and tests do not prove the truth of a deliverable.
- ENS and metadata are external dependencies. Optional job-page failures are bounded; identity availability and correct operational configuration still matter.
- The selected integrated compiler profile produces a 24,477-byte Manager runtime, leaving 99 bytes below Ethereum's 24,576-byte limit; see the [source-bound optimizer measurement](security/sol-2026-7-workaround.md#evidence-obtained). This build measurement is not a fresh observation of any deployed contract. Preserve the exact source and compiler settings and repeat bytecode/deployment checks after a source or compiler change.
- CI audits the complete root, deployment and UI dependency trees and rejects advisories at every severity. Repeat those checks against the current registry before deployment; a clean advisory database result does not prove absence of unknown vulnerabilities.

The [deploy-day runbook](DEPLOY_DAY_RUNBOOK.md), [owner controls](OWNER_CONTROLS.md) and [incident response](OPERATIONS/INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md) describe the operational steps.

# Private Fleet and dedicated Mac setup

<!-- Generated by scripts/docs/current-release.mjs from the companion edition map. -->

Public companion: **AGIJobManager 1.19.6**. Private editions: **Fleet 1.10.0, Agent 1.16.0, Node 2.17.0**. These private applications are delivered separately; cloning this repository does not install them.

## Transformation campaign inspection

Public v1.19.6 adds inert inspection of complete Alpha transformation campaigns through an installed compatible native inspector. Its current native pilot has zero currency allowances and cannot create a positive paid USDC proposal. It does not install, execute, commission or qualify a private Fleet runtime. Keep the existing Builder source pin, private editions and recovery journals. See [the transformation adapter boundary](../successor/TRANSFORMATIONAL_WORK.md) and [current release recovery](../releases/v1.19.6/RECOVERY_GUIDE.md).

## Choose the machine and role

| Machine or service | Role | Start page in the private download |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dedicated M1/M2 Mac mini | AGI Agent creates deliverables | Agent `START_HERE.html` |
| Dedicated M1 MacBook Pro or another Mac | AGI Node evaluates actual delivered work | Node `START_HERE.html` |
| Additional dedicated services | Employer, Evidence, Moderator and Recovery | Fleet `START_HERE.html` |

Keep signing and compute in separate Standard macOS accounts. On the Agent Mac, the existing account names `agiagentv0` and `agiagentcomputev0` can be retained. One wallet has one active signing writer and its original journal. Two Macs owned by one controller do not establish independent validation; exclude the Node's related Agent from its reviews.

Open the downloaded `START_HERE.html`, choose a role, and follow its setup and connection rehearsal. The private runtime requires its own Node.js version, currently 24.19+ within 24.x. The public repository's Node requirement applies to public build/deployment tooling.

## Upgrade without losing state

1. Stop intake and preserve a verified backup of every existing data directory and encrypted vault.
2. Reconcile pending transactions and old paid obligations. Keep claims, refunds, recovery policies, capacity reservations and cumulative spending.
3. Extract the new application separately, verify its manifest and point its launcher at the original data directory. Do not overwrite it with old application code.
4. Enroll freshly signed schema 6 participant / schema 7 employer `operator-budget` policies. Keep an existing review policy for recovery; the Node can also enroll its new review-spending budget.
5. Start observation, test the exact compute connection and supported delivery/review path, then activate the bounded commissioned scope.

The new-work workflow has no retainer funding or activation. Employer funding does not require a review-escrow policy. Existing escrow credits and refunds remain recoverable.

## Supported computer work and remaining commissioning

Two execution paths are included. The existing wallet workflow handles public inputs in an isolated Docker desktop/browser. The new private `workforce/` runner uses an authenticated OpenClaw node to perform screenshot, keyboard, pointer and accessibility actions in a dedicated native Mac account. It supports signed-in applications and scoped input/output files through encrypted task packets, immutable inputs, exact runtime grants and independent Node delivery review.

Open `Launch-Native-Workforce.command` and `docs/NATIVE_WORKFORCE.html` in the private download. Keep the operator grant key and wallet in a separate signing account. The native controller has authority over the whole dedicated OS account; resource labels and model instructions are not per-app or network confinement. Install only task accounts there. Native private workflows do not automatically post jobs, submit encrypted completion URIs or sign on-chain votes. The public publisher rejects scoped content before network publication. A private DAG coordinator schedules eligible Agent/Node stages, verifies signed receipts and routes rejections for separately admitted repair. See [confidential project work](CONFIDENTIAL_PROJECT_WORK.md).

The current OpenClaw profile pin is 2026.9.5; it is a reproducible baseline, not a claim that this is the newest available OpenClaw release. Review [current computer-use capabilities](COMPUTER_USE_CURRENT.md), then commission any changed model, provider, application or tool configuration before admitting its jobs. An account subscription alone does not demonstrate API/CLI access, capacity or an available billing path.

Use the [project economics planner](PROJECT_ECONOMICS.md) and [bounded pilot guide](VALUE_TIER_PILOT.md) before assigning multi-stage paid work. Current private packages include the same planner and three price-tier examples. The native adapter clears stale observations after a failed refresh.

The [workforce qualification gate](WORKFORCE_QUALIFICATION.md) requires signed, exact-source evidence for two real Macs, restart recovery, held-out validation, actual bills and useful cash settlements, supervision limits and independent security review. The separate pilot mode allows bounded, explicitly signed rehearsals; pilot results cannot become production qualification automatically.

Record actual provider costs, outcomes, false approvals/rejections, deadlines, recovery and human exception time. Local tests and historical simulations do not prove these on physical Macs. Each private package includes the detailed commissioning and rollback guides.

Later main-branch changes and candidate builds require separate qualification; they do not inherit the release evidence. The [previous published release v1.19.5](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGIJobManager/releases/tag/v1.19.5) remains available for historical comparison.

Checksums bind content; they do not establish GitHub-enforced immutability. Maintainers should [enable release immutability](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-your-supply-chain/establish-provenance-and-integrity/prevent-release-changes) before future releases and verify `immutable: true` in the published release metadata. Merging runs website validation but does not publish Pages. Software release publication requires a separate `workflow_dispatch` of the reviewed release publisher on the exact qualified main revision with confirmation `PUBLISH_v1.19.6`. Pages has two separate routes: the authenticated completion of that software publisher, or a maintainer dispatch after reviewing the applicable website checks with `publish: true` and `source_commit` equal to the reviewed main revision's full SHA. A mismatched or superseded SHA stops publication. Software publication does not authorize on-chain deployment or intake activation.

## Choose the creation route

For the owner-entered Ubuntu mainnet route, use the [hidden-prompt creator guide](deployment/ubuntu-ephemeral-creator.md). It takes the deployer key only through its local hidden prompt and rejects deployment dotenv files, secret environment values and secret arguments. Use a separate reviewed checkout without running the environment-backed setup below. The creator and Ledger governor are separate; governor configuration and activation remain separate actions.

## Prepare the environment-backed route

Use Node 22.23.2 for the public qualification/deployment workflow and the committed lockfiles. From the source root:

```bash
npm ci
npm --prefix hardhat ci
npm --prefix hardhat run setup
```

Review the generated private configuration and both settlement recipients, final owner, chain, native USDC and identity settings. See [the complete Hardhat procedure](../hardhat/README.md) and [every supported setting](DEPLOYMENT_CONFIGURATION.md). Private Fleet runtimes have their own Node requirements in their package guides.

## Commands from the source root

These command names are checked against the executable Hardhat package scripts. Plans explicitly select read-only mode; missing or empty DRY_RUN also defaults to read-only.

| Task | Command | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create private configuration | `npm --prefix hardhat run setup` | Offline; preserves existing files |
| Check mainnet profile | `npm --prefix hardhat run check:config:mainnet` | Offline; no signer or RPC |
| Check Sepolia profile | `npm --prefix hardhat run check:config:sepolia` | Offline; no signer or RPC |
| Compile pinned contracts | `npm --prefix hardhat run compile` | Local compiler; no chain transactions |
| Test preflight and recovery | `npm --prefix hardhat run test:preflight` | Local fixtures |
| Test compiler-derived registry | `npm --prefix hardhat run test:registry-native` | Pinned compiler and disposable local chain |
| Test actual local deployments | `npm --prefix hardhat run test:deployment` | Disposable local chain |
| Test historical native USDC | `npm --prefix hardhat run test:mainnet-fork` | Local fork; no public-chain broadcasts |
| Test USDC/ENS cutover | `npm --prefix hardhat run test:cutover` | Local fork; preserves historical evidence |
| Plan mainnet deployment | `DRY_RUN=1 npm --prefix hardhat run deploy:mainnet` | Explicit DRY_RUN=1; chain reads only |
| Plan Sepolia deployment | `DRY_RUN=1 npm --prefix hardhat run deploy:sepolia` | Explicit DRY_RUN=1; chain reads only |
| Plan mainnet ENS helper | `DRY_RUN=1 npm --prefix hardhat run deploy:ens-job-pages:mainnet` | Explicit DRY_RUN=1; chain reads only |
| Plan Sepolia ENS helper | `DRY_RUN=1 npm --prefix hardhat run deploy:ens-job-pages:sepolia` | Explicit DRY_RUN=1; chain reads only |
| Recover mainnet source verification | `npm --prefix hardhat run reverify:mainnet` | Chain reads and explorer requests; no chain broadcasts |
| Recover Sepolia source verification | `npm --prefix hardhat run reverify:sepolia` | Chain reads and explorer requests; no chain broadcasts |
| Recover existing review escrow on mainnet | `npm --prefix hardhat run recover:review-escrow:mainnet` | Read-only plan by default; existing address/journal required; no new deployment |
| Recover existing review escrow on Sepolia | `npm --prefix hardhat run recover:review-escrow:sepolia` | Read-only plan by default; existing address/journal required; no new deployment |

Manager verification recovery requires DEPLOYMENT_RECEIPT; existing review-escrow recovery instead requires REVIEW_ESCROW_ADDRESS and its original journal. Readiness additionally requires READINESS_NFT_CONFIG and, only for reviewed identity changes, READINESS_CONFIG. Relative environment paths use the Hardhat npm process directory; follow the configuration reference. A successful offline check does not validate a live instance.

## Authorize deployment and then intake separately

The environment-backed commands in this inventory require explicit DRY_RUN=0, the selected funded signer and explorer verification for actual deployment. Mainnet additionally requires DEPLOY_CONFIRM_MAINNET=I_UNDERSTAND_MAINNET_DEPLOYMENT. The recommended [Ubuntu hidden-prompt route](deployment/ubuntu-ephemeral-creator.md) has its own public-plan confirmation and recovery procedure; it does not use those secret-bearing environment settings. Follow the selected route after reviewing its exact source and plan; this command inventory does not authorize a broadcast.

Current-schema creation assigns the explicit governor atomically and starts the manager paused. Verify owner() equals the reviewed governor and pendingOwner() is zero; no creator handover or ownership acceptance is required. Preserve the journal and exact compiler input, finish verification and pass the actual instance's [launch checklist](LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md). Historical six-argument deployment records retain their original two-step handover; later voluntary Manager ownership changes also remain two-step. A failed command may already have broadcast; inspect receipts before retrying. Optional ENS helper creation has its own journal and leaves governor configuration in a separate action plan.

## Qualification boundaries

| Evidence | What it establishes | Separate evidence needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Release CI | Behavior of the pinned source and tested scenarios | Independent review and the actual operator setup |
| Hardhat readiness | Recorded contract code, owner, token, recipients, selected policies and reserve state | Other mutable policies, signer security, monitoring and participant operations |
| Economic admission | Signed assumptions and configured cost/capital/capacity limits | Observed employer value, actual costs and independent participants |
| Private Fleet commissioning | Rehearsed execution on the operator's actual machines and services | Sustained useful throughput and ongoing recovery measurements |

The existing manager and its payout rules are unchanged. New work uses [no-retainer operations](OPERATIONS/NO_RETAINERS.md). Existing AGIReviewEscrow records are retained for credit and refund recovery. The companion escrow script permits only source-verification recovery against its original journal; new escrow deployment is disabled. Publishing software does not open intake, qualify private hardware or establish production throughput. Manual console posting does not enforce [pre-funding qualification](OPERATIONS/PREFUNDING.md).

# Start here — AGIJobManager v1.19.6

**v1.19.6 maintenance candidate:** [review the dependency repair and validation boundary](releases/v1.19.6/START_HERE.md). Publication and exact-final-source qualification remain separate.

**[SUCCESSOR Ω Builder for everyone](successor/README.md)** · [Guide français](successor/GUIDE_FR.md): run two useful local missions, improve, download, restore and rerun without a wallet.

**Retained from v1.19.5:** [inspect an Alpha transformation campaign](releases/v1.19.5/START_HERE.md) through the developer API. The current native zero-currency pilot supports free inspection only. It cannot create a positive paid proposal or execute work. The existing local Builder remains the first path to useful browser output.

For the latest reported deployment, start with the [17 October Manager and authority record](deployments/MAINNET_MANAGER_2026-10-17.md). The [historical October 10 inspection and recovery workflow](OPERATIONS/COMMISSIONING.md#historical-manager-and-ens-helper--10-october-2026) selects only that earlier Manager and its ENS helper; its commands do not inspect the October 17 Manager.

The [retained 19 October ENS configuration addendum](deployments/ENS_CONFIGURATION_RETAINED_2026-10-19.md) adds the subsequent helper/root/prefix snapshot, the historical block timestamp, the fee exception and separate unresolved explorer source review. It changes no transaction target or activation authority.

## Have an idea? Start with a simple request

**[Start my request — English →](https://montrealai.github.io/AGIJobManager/employers/)** · **[Commencer ma demande — français →](https://montrealai.github.io/AGIJobManager/fr/employers/)**

Want a website, a presentation, a report or help comparing your options? Choose an example, describe what you need, then save, download or print your request. The page uses everyday words, large buttons and a **Larger text / Texte agrandi** option. You can take your time and return to a request saved in the same browser.

**Preparation is free, with no sign-up or wallet required.** Posting and payment are a separate, advanced step that currently needs a digital wallet, USDC and ETH for network fees. Nothing is posted or paid for on the preparation page. [Read the employer guide](ui/EMPLOYER_ONBOARDING.md) when you are ready for the next step.

## For participants and operators

AGI Jobs covers work a person or team can do using a keyboard, mouse and screen. New automated work uses [operator-budget admission without retainers](OPERATIONS/NO_RETAINERS.md): schema 6 for Agents/Nodes and schema 7 for employers. Preserve existing escrow credits, refunds and journals. Read [computer work and present runtime coverage](OPERATIONS/GENERAL_COMPUTER_WORK.md).

**Deployment entrypoint:** [release identity and checked commands](RELEASE_GUIDE.md).

Before signing, verify the actual deployment operator, fees and service terms. The [legal center](LEGAL/README.md) explains publisher/owner roles, privacy and risk. The console's fresh acknowledgement is a local safeguard, not an operator agreement or regulatory clearance.


Read [what this release includes and how existing managers remain compatible](V1_RELEASE_SCOPE.md). [Current release behavior and evidence](V1_RELEASE_SCOPE.md#published-download-versus-current-source).

AGIJobManager holds a job's USDC payment until the work reaches a settlement outcome. Employers post work, eligible agents take jobs, validators assess the submitted evidence, and moderators handle disputes. The owner configures the instance and can pause it.

**This download supplies software, not a running marketplace.** A deployment operator must deploy and verify the manager, configure its owner and two recipients, arrange eligible participants, and open intake. No live manager address or recipient wallets are supplied.

AGI Agents normally qualify through a name under `agent.agi.eth` or `alpha.agent.agi.eth`; AGI Validators through `club.agi.eth` or `alpha.club.agi.eth`. The connected wallet must satisfy the configured name's NameWrapper ownership/approval or resolver-address check. Enter only the label, such as `alice`. The contract preserves owner-managed `additionalAgents`/`additionalValidators` and role-specific Merkle proofs as explicit membership exceptions; those routes are not proof of ENS membership. Agents also need a qualifying enabled NFT when the job’s posting-time NFT requirement is on. Fresh v1.13.0 managers start with that requirement disabled; owners can enable it for future jobs. These participant identity checks are separate from optional ENS job-page metadata.

## Choose your next step

| Your goal | Start with | What you need |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Prepare your first request | [English guided page](https://montrealai.github.io/AGIJobManager/employers/) or [page guidée en français](https://montrealai.github.io/AGIJobManager/fr/employers/) | An idea and a browser; no wallet or software installation to prepare |
| Inspect a native Alpha transformation campaign | [v1.19.5 start guide](releases/v1.19.5/START_HERE.md), then [adapter contract](successor/TRANSFORMATIONAL_WORK.md) | Original public campaign, installed compatible native inspector and independently supplied expected runtime bindings; no wallet for inspection |
| Post, perform or validate a job | [USDC console guide](ui/GENESIS_JOB_MAINNET_HTML_UI.md), then [participant guide](USERS.md) | A verified deployed manager, the correct wallet, USDC and ETH for gas |
| See how a real job would proceed | [Genesis artwork worked example](examples/GENESIS_JOB_TODAY.md) | Read the participant steps, cost tables, review timing and recovery branches |
| Deploy the software | [Launch checklist](LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md), then [Hardhat guide](../hardhat/README.md) | Reviewed configuration, both recipients, intended owner and a testnet rehearsal |
| Operate an existing instance | [Owner runbook](OWNER_RUNBOOK.md) | The accepted owner wallet and verified on-chain configuration |
| Respond to a problem | [Incident response](OPERATIONS/INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md) | Manager address, chain, transaction hashes and current pause/reserve state |
| Evaluate the release | [Mainnet readiness](MAINNET_READINESS.md) and [testing](TESTING.md) | Source, release manifest, checksums and the linked CI evidence |

Check [release and download availability for v1.19.6](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGIJobManager/releases/tag/v1.19.6) on the repository's matching release page. Check its `SHA256SUMS.txt` before use. Open `agijobmanager-usdc.html` in a browser with an Ethereum wallet. It needs internet access for the integrity-pinned Web3 library, wallet/RPC communication and display resources; it is not an offline transaction application. Never enter a seed phrase or private key into the console. Public submissions must contain no added personal information, confidential material or secrets; read the [user-data rules](LEGAL/USER_DATA_RULES.md). Draft saving is explicit and unencrypted. Review each public-content confirmation before an upload or submission.

For a practical cost comparison, operators can run `npm run economics:check -- --example`, then replace its hypothetical assumptions with their own scenario. See [economics](game-theory.md).

## Understand the payment before signing

For a successful **100 USDC** job with the default 8% validator budget and qualifying approval votes:

| Paid in this order | Amount from the original job cost |
| --- | ---: |
| Correct-side validators | 8 USDC total |
| First configured wallet | 30 USDC |
| Second configured wallet | 10 USDC |
| Assigned agent | 52 USDC |

The 30% and 10% shares are fixed and included in the job cost. The owner can set the validator percentage to 1–60% for future postings; every posted job retains its rate. Bond deposits, refunds and slashing are accounted separately. Integer rounding and unallocated rewards are described in the [payout specification](USDC_PAYOUT_SPLIT.md). USDC uses six decimals; ETH is required for gas.

After the full review and any later approval challenge, finalization with no votes, insufficient participation, or a tie opens a dispute and pays nobody. Only explicit buyer acceptance or an authorized agent-win decision can pay unreviewed work; with no validators, the agent receives the 60% remainder. Voting, expiry, finalization and refunds require transactions; elapsed time alone never sends money. [See what to do if work is missing or poor](BUYER_PROTECTION.md).

## Complete one job

Need an agent credential? The console’s **Get free name + identity NFT** option uses `FreeTrialSubdomainRegistrarIdentity` to register both an `*.alpha.agent.agi.eth` name and a soulbound Alpha Agent Identity NFT for your connected wallet. Registration is free; Ethereum gas is separate. Validity lasts up to 30 days, capped by the parent expiry. Check the live preview: an NFT can remain visible after the credential expires. The separate ENS-only option does not create this identity NFT. Read [identity and job eligibility](guides/IDENTITY_AND_PROOFS.md#free-alpha-agent-name-and-identity-nft) before applying; buyers do not need this credential. If the owner enables this ENS root and NFT collection, these free credentials can qualify you to take jobs without an additional paid identity. Bonds and gas still apply, and payment follows successful settlement. Follow the [agent guide](roles/AGENT.md) from registration through payment.

1. **Employer:** write the scope, acceptance criteria and evidence requirements; choose a USDC cost and duration. Confirm the deployed manager and both recipients, approve only the required USDC, then post the job. Approval alone does not create a job. Save its ID and transaction hash.
2. **Agent:** confirm eligibility, the job’s recorded NFT requirement and any required credential, the posted payment and current bond. The first eligible successful application assigns the job; the employer does not choose among an application queue. Approve the required bond and apply. The duration starts on assignment.
3. **Agent:** finish the work and submit its completion URI before the assignment deadline. The URI identifies evidence; it does not itself prove quality.
4. **Validators:** review the work, confirm eligibility and the bond, then approve or disapprove during the review period. A validator can vote once per job. Votes can lead to approval, a dispute or a later finalization outcome.
5. **Any caller:** after the applicable review/challenge conditions are satisfied, submit finalization. For a disputed job, follow the moderator or stale-dispute owner path. Inspect the receipt, job state and USDC transfers; the UI simulation is a precheck, not a promise of inclusion or success.

The employer can cancel before assignment. Expiry requires an assigned job whose duration has elapsed without a completion request. A completion request instead enters review/dispute rules. [Participant guidance](USERS.md) and [lifecycle reference](PROTOCOL_FLOW.md) explain these branches.

## If a transaction does not finish

- **Wallet/network changed:** return to the intended account and Ethereum mainnet, reload state and review again. Do not reuse a stale confirmation.
- **Approval succeeded but the job action failed:** no job action occurred merely because approval succeeded. Check allowance and on-chain state before retrying; revoke unused allowance if abandoning the action.
- **Transaction pending or receipt unavailable:** inspect its hash on the correct chain before sending a replacement. An RPC timeout is not proof that the transaction failed.
- **Paused manager or changed terms:** read the current pause flags, limits, bond and job state. Ask the operator to resolve the cause; do not change networks or approve another token to bypass it.
- **USDC paused or a recipient blocked:** failed outgoing payments stay reserved for the original beneficiary. Other eligible recipients can still be paid. Use **Retry my payment** after the issuer restriction resolves; wallet rotation cannot redirect existing entitlements.

Only a successful receipt and verified resulting state establish the outcome. Source review, an independent operational security review and instance-specific [readiness checks](MAINNET_READINESS.md) remain necessary for a high-stakes launch.

## Check conditional economics

Before committing more work, use the [offline screening guide](OPERATIONS/ECONOMIC_SCREENING.md) to compare costs, employer value, outcome weights and participant loss limits. Run `npm run economics:screen -- --example` from the source root. The example is hypothetical and a successful screen does not authorize a transaction.

For autonomous integration, read [qualified admission](OPERATIONS/QUALIFIED_ADMISSION.md). Start with `npm run economics:lifecycle -- --example`; hypothetical examples do not authorize paid work.

For automated employer intake, start with [pre-funding qualification](OPERATIONS/PREFUNDING.md). Manual console posting does not perform this check.

## Native workforce readiness

The private companions include dedicated-account native execution and encrypted handoffs. Use [private setup](OPERATIONS/PRIVATE_FLEET.md) and [the signed operational evidence gate](OPERATIONS/WORKFORCE_QUALIFICATION.md) before production. Publication is not physical commissioning or independent assurance.

The ENS membership correction introduced in v1.17.0 rejects unowned-name and stale-wrapper admission paths. The [engineering finding](qualification/ENS_MEMBERSHIP_REVOCATION.md) describes the scope and verification limits. The current integrated source retains that membership correction alongside explicit-governor construction and its selected compiler optimizer mitigation; original deployment bytecode and records remain separate. ## Included in this edition

- Public source and a versioned USDC console with participant, owner and recovery guidance.
- Inert full-campaign inspection through the installed Alpha native inspector, with independently supplied runtime bindings. The current native zero-currency pilot supports free inspection only; positive paid proposals are unsupported.
- Eight fixed library links, USDC accounting, buyer protections and reserved payment claims, including the inherited ENS authorization correction described above.
- Hardhat setup, explicit read-only plans, guarded deployment, source verification, transaction journals, recovery and instance-readiness checks.
- Lifecycle economics, signed action-bound qualification, pre-funding offer/capacity checks and canonical state/closure observations.
- Reproducible release assets, source qualification, per-file manifests and asset checksums.

| Does the work meet the buyer's needs? | Measurable acceptance criteria, accessible deliverables and independent inspection |
| Are different participants actually independent? | Conflict disclosures and operating controls beyond wallet and credential comparisons |
| Is participation economically worthwhile? | Actual work, review, gas and capital costs across successful, disputed and unpaid outcomes |
| Can a newcomer use the complete journey? | Observed user sessions; automated browser tests do not substitute for them |
| Is this particular instance ready for paid jobs? | Verified signers, recipients, policy, participants, monitoring and an actual readiness report |
| Has the release received external assurance? | A separately obtained independent security and economic review; internal reviews do not provide this |

Owner pauses can delay exits; USDC issuer restrictions can delay transfers; unavailable arbitration can leave honest work unpaid after neutral refund. Final settlement has no built-in chargeback, revision round or partial settlement. Read [buyer protection](BUYER_PROTECTION.md) and [economics](game-theory.md) before committing funds.

## Put the release into use

Start with [the participant guide](START_HERE.md), run the [observed acceptance journeys](V1_ACCEPTANCE.md), and keep the actual instance's [launch checklist](LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md) with its evidence. The release validation record describes what was executed for the source; it must not be copied as proof of a live instance.

The qualification approach follows layered testing, access-control review and operational precautions described in [Ethereum's smart-contract security guidance](https://ethereum.org/developers/docs/smart-contracts/security/). Native USDC addresses must be checked against [Circle's current registry](https://developers.circle.com/stablecoins/usdc-contract-addresses).

## Current admission primitives

The public tools cover explicit lifecycle stress cases, operator-owned economic limits, signed evidence attestations, and current canonical two-RPC terms. They do not implement an autonomous signing service or certify market inputs. See [qualified admission](OPERATIONS/QUALIFIED_ADMISSION.md) and [current pre-funding and closure scope](OPERATIONS/PREFUNDING.md).

# USDC standalone console v1.19.6

v1.19.3 retains the v1.0.5 protocol notices unchanged and links the [legal center](../LEGAL/README.md). Acknowledgement starts unchecked, is never restored from browser storage, and must be renewed after account/network/manager changes or page restoration. Withdrawing acknowledgement also cancels a pending transaction review. This is a local safeguard; the operator must supply its own legally appropriate service terms and acceptance process. The console retains the v1.0.5 separate public-content check for publishing text/links and IPFS uploads. It does not scan for every personal detail or restrict direct contract calls.


Use the [matching release status and assets](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGIJobManager/releases/tag/v1.19.6) with an independently verified, compatible USDC Manager on Ethereum mainnet. Start with the [October 17 reported Manager and its evidence limits](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGIJobManager/blob/d5d4ad93f00a3dfe6439b0f32edb1a2fcf70e0c2/docs/deployments/MAINNET_MANAGER_2026-10-17.md), then explicitly select and verify the intended transaction target. This dated, owner-reported snapshot is not a fresh live-state or ABI qualification. No manager is configured by default. Already verified compatible v0.9.6 instances can keep their original jobs and interfaces; this interface update does not require or perform their redeployment.

The [v1.19.6 transformation inspection API](../successor/TRANSFORMATIONAL_WORK.md) is separate from this console. Its native zero-currency pilot cannot create a positive paid proposal, execute work or authorize signing. The existing Builder and all historical deployment evidence remain preserved.

The [current repository console](../../ui/agijobmanager-usdc.html) includes clear cost and buyer guidance and requires `getJobBonds` for voting. v0.9.5 and older managers do not have that getter. See [compatibility and verification](../qualification/BUYER_ECONOMICS_FOLLOWUP.md), including the older console's bond-quote limitation. Existing jobs remain on their original contracts.

The repository console has post-release context/mobile fixes and a **Get free name + identity NFT** action that the frozen v1.0.0 asset does not contain. [Choose a version and download the pinned reviewed console](../V1_RELEASE_SCOPE.md#published-download-versus-current-source). Read the [agent journey](../roles/AGENT.md) for registration, expiry, job eligibility and payment.

Before enabling writes the console checks chain ID 1, contract code, the manager's immutable `usdcToken()` address and six decimals. It repeats these checks before each transaction. Token identity checks do not prove source correctness; verify the deployment independently first.

All amounts use USDC with at most six decimal places. Excess precision is rejected. Approval, escrow, bonds, settlement and withdrawals use the same USDC address. The old bridge/vault panel is retired, and saved forms and wallet context retain the v0.9.6 namespace because the ABI and deployed runtime remain compatible; the disabled fresh NFT-admission default introduced in v1.0.3 is preserved. The console still rechecks account, chain and manager before writing. Pre-v0.9.6 saved context is not imported.

Wallet/account/chain changes invalidate reviews and write eligibility. Review the exact amount and spender before signing; USDC approval is separate from a job transaction. ETH is required only for gas.

See [the migration guide](../USDC_MIGRATION.md) for supported chains, default economics, transfer restrictions and deployment steps. Prior consoles remain in the v0.4.0 Git tag for historical operations.

## Keep private information out of public content

Follow the [user-data rules](../LEGAL/USER_DATA_RULES.md). Review the exact transaction fields or upload JSON; do not add personal information, confidential work, access tokens or private sharing links. The operator and each participant retain their actual statutory duties.

Typing no longer saves builder drafts. Use **Save draft on this device** and **Load saved draft** deliberately. Completion drafts are memory-only. **Clear saved job content** removes old saved drafts and notes on this browser origin. Saved notes/drafts are unencrypted; downloads and public copies are separate. Pinning credentials are masked, never saved/restored, and cleared after upload/review. Only the HTTPS Pinata origin receives Pinata JWTs; custom endpoints receive JSON without them. See the [privacy/storage guide](../privacy-and-storage.md).
